processing: A flavoured blend on the Earl Grey model: black tea scented with bergamot, plus a creamy flavouring. Exact recipes belong to each blender, and little is documented about them.
harvest_season: Not tied to a harvest: as with other flavoured blends, the base tea is bought in and blended all year.
appearance_dry: Typically dark, twisted black leaf, sometimes with flower petals, as in other Earl Grey blends.
appearance_liquor: Clear reddish amber, typical of a medium black tea.
taste_profile: Expect the citrus of bergamot softened by a sweet, creamy note, over the plain body of black tea; how strong each is depends on the blender.

brewing.notes: Brew Western-style, as with other Earl Grey blends. Taste at three minutes; longer steeps bring out tannin over the flavouring.

vintage_note: Not sold by year or season, as is usual for flavoured blends: it is a shop blend sold year-round. Scented teas tend to lose aroma with time, so buy small amounts and use them while fragrant.
description:
Earl Grey Cream, also spelled Creme, is a recognised style among tea drinkers: Earl Grey with a creamy flavour layered over the bergamot. It is a family of shop blends with no single recipe, and little is documented about any fixed standard.

The structure follows other flavoured blends. A black base is scented with bergamot and given a creamy flavouring. There is no cream in the tin, and the label is what tells you which flavourings were used.

In the cup, you should get citrus first and a soft sweetness behind it. Brew it like any Earl Grey, then decide whether it needs anything: the creamy note often makes milk feel optional.

When buying, read the ingredients and smell it if you can. As with any flavoured tea, a blend that is all perfume and no tea is the common disappointment. A plain Earl Grey alongside it is the easiest way to judge what the extra flavouring adds.
history: Little is documented about where or when this variation first appeared. It sits among the many modern flavoured variations on Earl Grey and is known today as a style name used by tea sellers, without a recorded creator.
